limits: Different W3 profiles use different independently learned histories; profile subtraction is not a single-stage contribution.
Range and median differences are not additive. Stage traces are pointwise additive.
No data-driven result alone proves physical displacement or absence of device disturbance.
Historical 3-night training uses only22–02; use/learn flags and gain do not enforce final output flatness or point-specific physical correctness.

direct_old_diagnostic_crosscheck.scope: Only matched X arrays used as independent evidence. No old executable run; old comments about mm/Y were not assumed true.

key_conclusions: All three devices had 3 historical nights, modes ready and baseline support; no frame-level solve failure or residual2.5 outlier rejection explains the remaining pattern.
ZXJ6 is used but not learned: spread screening removes it from learning; its regression load is applied with gain1. The modal core already produces the dominant negative late offset.
The three historical nights are22-02 learning windows, not full-night coverage. Existing modes are not refreshed at02:00 once available.

The historical energy guard permits residual energy below raw even when the output reverses sign or retains a large offset. It only applies to ordinary nonlearn regression rows, not the four learned target points or intentional J fit-only rows.
Removing each of the five largest live donor contributions leaves the ZXJ6 offset large. These fixed-model interventions do not identify a single dominant bad observation.

Existing no-W3 output somewhat reduces the residual but changes both history and live preprocessing; it does not remove the same old modal issue and is not a causal single-stage replacement recommendation.
